title: YOU WILL ONLY WEAR YOURSELVES OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses' father-in-law replied, 'What you are doing is not good. You and these
people who come to you will only wear yourselves out. The work is too heavy for
you; you cannot handle it alone.'" - Ex 18:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"What you are doing is not good."

That is a bold thing to say to the man who parted the sea. And notice what
Jethro identifies as not good: not laziness, not sin, but overwork in a genuinely
worthy cause.

Read his reasoning. "You and these people who come to you will only wear
yourselves out." Both suffer. The leader burns out, and the people receive worse
service than they should. Nobody wins in an unsustainable arrangement.

Then the sentence that matters most: "you cannot handle it alone."

This is not an insult. It is an accurate description of a human being. Moses was
not failing; he was finite. God made us with limits, and those limits are not
defects to be overcome by determination.

Elijah discovered this under a broom tree, and God's first response was to let
him sleep and give him food (1 Kgs 19:5-6). Jesus Himself withdrew from crowds
to rest and pray (Luke 5:16).

If you are exhausted in good work, hear this verse gently. The problem may not
be your commitment. It may be that you were never designed to carry it alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you treating your limits as a weakness to push through?
2. Who is being underserved because you are stretched too thin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that my limits are not failures. Help me to accept that I
cannot do this alone. Amen.
